subject: Building R under Windows using the MS toolchain

messages.author: 75162259159813e2
messages.subject: Building R under Windows using the MS toolchain
parts:
Dear list,
I wonder if this the right place to ask the question that follows. Apologies if it's not the case.

In our SW development team we have some libraries written in MATLAB that we would like to port to R.

Since maintaining a R code version from scratch is a very time consuming task, we came up with the idea of compiling the MATLAB code into a C library which would then be linked and called in R. Trouble is, GCC is currently not supported by the MATLAB tools, while the Visual Studio toolchain is, so we would need to be able to build R-compatible libraries using Visual Studio which, in turn, is apparently not compatible with RTools and Rcpp. So, here are my questions:

1) Has anybody out there ever endeavored to build the R source using the VS toolchain?

2) Might the upcoming R Tools for Visual Studio be of some help in this regard? I understand RTVS is mainly a VS-based IDE (akin to RStudio), but perhaps there's more under the hood...?

Any insight/help/ideas/links will be highly appreciated.

Thanks in advance and best regards,
Emmanuele Sordini

messages.author: 149440eddb848db9
messages.subject: Re: Building R under Windows using the MS toolchain
parts:
Hi, Emmanuele

As far as I know, it is not possible to build R from source using Microsoft tools, as you point out. The R build chain requires GCC, and I don't know of any work on integrating any other compilers.

As you point out,RTVS was recently announced (http://blog.revolutionanalytics.com/2016/01/r-coming-to-visual-studio.html). I can't comment on the behalf of the RTVS team, but my understanding is that RTVS allows you to use Visual Studio as your IDE for R. This will not solve your problem to compile R using the Microsoft compiler tool chain.

Andrie
